Annulus_Pressure_Psi: Surface iron rigged up and verified; wellhead isolated prior to opening frac valves.
Automated hydraulic valves open on the frac manifold and wellhead. Crews verify valve positions and confirm zero leaks.
Pumps engage at low rate to fill surface lines and perform a brief high-pressure pop-off/line test before breaking down the well.
Pump rate increases; surface treating pressure spikes sharply until the rock fractures, followed by a sudden pressure drop (breakdown) as fluid enters the formation.
Diluted hydrochloric acid (~15% HCl) hits the perforations, dissolving cement residue and near-wellbore scale to lower injection pressure and equalize flow across clusters.
High-rate, proppant-free slickwater or gel (80-100+ bpm) is pumped to initiate and widen the primary fracture network and overcome fluid leakoff into the rock.
Blender augers start feeding 100-mesh sand into the fluid stream at 0.5 lbs/gal to initiate fracture packing.
100-mesh proppant concentration steps up to 1.0 lbs/gal to build near-wellbore and far-field conductivity.
Biodegradable chemical diverter pills are dropped mid-stage at 15 ppt to temporarily plug dominant perforations and force fluid into under-stimulated clusters.
Switched to 40/70-mesh sand and stepped concentration up to 2.0 lbs/gal to pack primary fractures.
40/70-mesh proppant concentration reaches peak tail-in concentration of 3.0 lbs/gal to maximize near-wellbore conductivity.
Sand augers shut off; clean water with friction reducer is pumped to push the remaining sand slurry out of the casing and through the perforations.
All high-pressure pumps throttle down to idle and kick out of gear; flow rate hits 0 bpm.
Master frac valves close immediately to trap pressure downhole. Engineers record the Instantaneous Shut-In Pressure (ISIP) at 5,610 psi.
5-minute post-shut-in pressure recorded to evaluate fracture closure behavior and leakoff rate.
10-minute post-shut-in pressure recorded to monitor ongoing pressure dissipation.
15-minute post-shut-in pressure recorded completing standard falloff diagnostics.
The well is officially turned back over to the wireline crew to begin the next stage cycle (Stage N + 1).
